svg.text: PART A - tile counter cell (instantiate 2x: X axis and Y axis)
PART B - in-field test, tile address, RAM fetch (Fig 7 copy V port B) and colour select
Fig 11 - Maze Tile Renderer: pixel (x, y) -> tile address -> wall / floor colour
24 px tiles, 20 x 20 = 480 x 480 playfield at the left of the 640 x 480 screen. No divider: tile column / row are small counters that step in sync with x / y.
X axis: step = pix_ce, restart = h_end (Fig 8)
Y axis: step = line_tick, restart = line_tick & v_end (Fig 8)
Why this works: step and restart arrive in the same clock as x / y change,
so sub_q / tile_q are exactly aligned with the pixel (no lag).
sub_q wraps 23 -> 0 and bumps tile_q (tile_q = x / 24 without a divider).
restart (end of line / frame) clears both to 0.
tile_q is 6 bits: the blanking interval counts up to 33 (800 / 24).
Net labels: 'wrap' = output of sub_q == 23. 'step' / 'restart' are the same net
everywhere they appear (drawn as labels to avoid long crossing wires).
vga_tile_addr[8:0] -> Fig 7 copy V, port B
tile_addr = row * 20 + col = (row << 4) + (row << 2) + col (shifts are free wiring; two small adders, no multiplier)
wall flag = in_field & (tile != 0) - same definition as the collision engine (Fig 6b)
